title: Chapter test: Smart Pointers
summary: Twelve questions on Box, Deref, Drop, Rc, RefCell and Weak. You need 70% to pass; you can retry and your best score is kept.

questions.q: Which type lets a recursive enum have a known size?

questions.explanation: 2 is dropped early, then 3 and 1 in reverse order at the end.

options: Convention: it signals a cheap count increment, not a deep copy
questions.explanation: Both do the same thing for Rc.

questions.q: After `let a = Rc::new(1); let b = Rc::clone(&a); let c = Rc::clone(&b); drop(b);`, what is `Rc::strong_count(&a)`?

options: at run time, panicking on violation
questions.explanation: That is the trade it makes for flexibility.

options: `let c = RefCell::new(1); let a = c.borrow(); let b = c.borrow();`
`let c = RefCell::new(1); let a = c.borrow(); let b = c.borrow_mut();`
questions.explanation: A mutable borrow while a shared borrow is alive.

questions.q: Shared mutable state in single-threaded code is usually written as...
questions.explanation: Rc for owners, RefCell for mutation.

questions.q: Two nodes hold `Rc` pointers to each other and their variables go out of scope. What happens?
options: Neither is freed: a memory leak
questions.explanation: Each still has one strong owner.

questions.q: What does `Weak::upgrade` return when the value has been dropped?
questions.explanation: That is why it returns an Option.

questions.q: Which are not usable across threads?
questions.explanation: Their counters and borrow flags are not synchronized; use Arc and Mutex.
